content.title: About
content.content: The fried fish sandwich is a fast‑food item consisting of a bun filled with a piece of breaded and deep‑fried fish, often topped with sauce, lettuce, and other vegetables. It has been a popular quick‑serve snack in the United States since the late 18th century.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first fried fish sandwich was introduced in 1793 at one of the earliest American fast‑food establishments.
Traditionally white fish such as cod or pollock is used, though regional variations may feature other species.
In the U.S. it is commonly served with tartar sauce or a lemon‑mayonnaise dressing.
Some countries refer to a similar product as a “fish burger,” where the fish is formed into a patty.
The rise of plant‑based alternatives in the 2020s led to vegan versions made from soy or pea protein.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fried fish provides a complete source of animal protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: When fatty fish such as salmon is used, the sandwich can supply heart‑healthy omega‑3s.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish is rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Selenium and iodine in fish contribute to thyroid health and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the bun and fats from the fish offers a fast source of energy.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories and saturated fat, which may be undesirable in excess.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to fish or seafood.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Fish can contain mercury or other heavy metals; sourcing from reputable suppliers is recommended.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Condiments often contain high sodium levels, which can affect blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is typically eaten hot, split in half. It pairs well with fresh lettuce, pickles, tomato slices, and a squeeze of lemon. For a lighter option, use a whole‑grain bun or bake the fish instead of frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sandwich should be refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours. Keep the fried fish in an airtight container to prevent odor absorption. Reheat in an oven or air‑fryer rather than a microwave to retain crispness.
